answer.rationale: A release deployed 2 hours ago coincides with p99 latency climbing 5x above target over 90 minutes during peak settlement load. Memory_b1 demonstrates rollback cleared a checkout error spike without customer impact when a recent build was the culprit. Memory_b6 shows staged gating catches regressions early. The timing and magnitude of degradation strongly suggest the release introduced latency regression. Verifying memory_b1 confirms rollback safety and speed. Rollback is the highest-confidence single intervention because: (1) it directly removes the suspected source, (2) it has precedent for fast recovery without write loss, (3) it avoids risky capacity/routing choices during peak settlement. Regional failover and circuit breakers are defensive but don't address root cause. Read replica routing won't help write path latency. Capacity add is slow to provision. Rollback lets us recover immediately while preserving full write traffic and the option to investigate the release post-incident. If rollback doesn't resolve it, we have memory_b3 (provisioning) and memory_b2 (failover) for follow-up actions.
